Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Concludes Bizzchitra Photography Competition – Edition 3
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited successfully concluded the Bizzchitra Photography Competition – Edition 3 on 2082/11/01, organized to celebrate World Photography Day. The competition, held from Bhadra 11 to Ashwin 31, 2082, invited photographers to capture images reflecting local small and medium businesses, promoting entrepreneurship and positive messages through photography.
A three-member jury selected 15 outstanding photos, with awards presented in Kathmandu for first, second, and third places. Suyog Kunwar won first place (Rs. 25,000), Paras Bajracharya second (Rs. 20,000), and Devananda Pokharel third (Rs. 15,000). Sharman Raj Bhandari received the Public Choice Award (Rs. 10,000). Certificates were also distributed to the top 15 photographers.
The edition featured increased prize amounts compared to previous years, reflecting the bank’s commitment to promoting local businesses, entrepreneurship, and art. The event coincided with the bank’s Mahalaxmi Magh Mahotsav, aimed at enhancing digital banking services and encouraging secure, cashless transactions.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Advances Social and Economic Development Through CSR
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has actively carried out various corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives across health, education, disaster management, environment, culture, infrastructure, and community development.
Highlights include funding a health camp at Shree Gandhakuti Vihar, Lalitpur; providing road furniture with traffic signs to manage parking and road safety in collaboration with the Traffic Police, Maharajgunj; distributing sewing machines in Humla for skill development and economic empowerment; and supporting the construction of a playground at Shree Bhanu Secondary School, Rupandehi. The bank believes these initiatives contribute to overall economic and social development.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Launches “Magh Mahotsav” to Promote Digital Banking
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has launched “Mahalaxmi Magh Mahotsav”, a digital promotion campaign for the month of Magh 2082 to encourage safe, convenient, and cashless banking transactions. As part of the initiative, the bank is offering higher interest rates on fixed deposits opened through its mobile app “Mahalaxmi Smart Sathi,” along with full fee waivers on debit cards, mobile banking registration, and credit card issuance and annual fees.
Customers can also enjoy cashback on pharmacy bill payments made via the mobile app and free registration for the “Koili” audio payment notification service. The campaign aims to expand access to digital banking, reduce the need for in-branch visits, and further promote digital transactions across the country.

Headline: MLBL Launches Special Gold & Silver Loan to Celebrate New Year 2026
Full Content:
On the occasion of the English New Year 2026, Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has announced a revised Loan Against Bullion (Gold & Silver) facility with special benefits for customers. This facility offers competitive interest rates, a simple and secure process, and loans up to NPR 50 lakh against gold or silver purchased from authorized dealers.
The service is available through select branches in Kathmandu, Pokhara, Maharajgunj, Hetauda, and Bhairahawa, while applications can be submitted at any branch. MLBL emphasizes customer convenience and financial management, continuing its mission of quality banking for over 31 years with more than 800,000 customers nationwide.

Headline: Rajesh Upadhyay Re-elected as MLBL Chairman, Takes Oath of Office
Full Content:
At its 24th Annual General Meeting, Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) appointed Mr. Rajesh Upadhyay as the new Chairperson.
He took the oath of office and secrecy on 2082/09/23 before Deputy Governor Mr. Bam Bahadur Mishra of Nepal Rastra Bank, in the presence of senior bank officials. The board also approved a proposal to distribute a 10.37% dividend.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Concludes 24th AGM, Approves 10.37% Dividend
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited held its 24th Annual General Meeting on 21 Poush 2082 under the chairmanship of Rajesh Upadhyay. The AGM approved the bank’s financial statements for FY 2081/82, including profit and loss, cash flow, and equity changes. A total dividend of 10.37% was declared, comprising 5.37% cash dividend and 5% bonus shares.
The bank reported improved financial indicators compared to FY 2080/81, with deposit reaching Rs. 56.22 Arba, loans NPR 47.21 Arba, and capital adequacy rising to 17.06%. Six directors were elected, three from founders and three from public shareholders, with Rajesh Upadhyay re-elected as Chairman. The AGM emphasized enhanced customer satisfaction and quality financial services.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Advances Community Development Through CSR Initiatives
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) implemented various Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) programs in FY 2082/83, focusing on financial literacy, education, health, disaster management, environment, culture, infrastructure, sustainable development, and welfare activities.
Highlights include organizing health camps and workshops for senior citizens in Humla, providing computers and tables to a damaged police post in Kathmandu, and supporting marginalized communities with food aid. The bank also funded modern toilets in schools across Baglung, Jhapa, and other districts, distributed winter clothing to 180 students in Lalitpur, and provided educational materials to students in Gorkha. These initiatives aim to contribute to overall economic and social development.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Wins International Award for Banking Innovation and Customer Excellence
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has been honored with the “Excellence in Banking Innovation and Customer Delight” award at the India Business Awards 2025 held in New Delhi on December 7, 2025. The award recognizes the bank’s innovations in banking services, strong leadership, brand reputation, customer trust, media presence, and corporate social responsibility.
MLBL, actively involved in cross-border financial services between India and Nepal, expects this recognition to strengthen Nepal-India banking relations and promote trade and remittances. Recently, the bank was also recognized by the Indian Chamber of Commerce (ICC), highlighting its growing international presence.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Partners with Coffee Chains to Offer Special Discounts to Customers
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has partnered with Arabica Coffee and Caffeophilia Bhaisepati to offer special discounts to its debit card, credit card, and mobile banking users. Customers can enjoy up to 15% discount at multiple Arabica Coffee outlets across Kathmandu and Lalitpur, 10% on coffee and hot beverages, and 15% on Italian food.
At Caffeophilia Bhaisepati, users will receive up to 10% discount on all services except bakery items. The bank believes this collaboration will directly benefit its customers and enhance their digital banking experience. MLBL has also recently introduced a facility allowing credit card users to purchase tour packages through various travel agencies and convert the amount into easy monthly installments payable over 6 to 12 months.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Partners with Daraz Nepal for 11.11 Campaign Offering Special Discounts
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has partnered with Daraz Nepal for the global 11.11 shopping campaign, offering special discounts and digital benefits to its customers. The collaboration aligns with the bank’s goal of expanding its digital banking services and enhancing customer engagement through online platforms.
Under this offer, valid from Kartik 25 to Mangsir 5, 2082, customers can enjoy exclusive discounts when shopping on Daraz using Mahalaxmi Bank cards. Debit card users will receive a 15% discount (up to Rs. 1,500), while credit card users will get a 20% discount (up to Rs. 2,000). Customers must collect vouchers from the Daraz platform to avail of the offer, which will be provided on a first-come, first-served basis.
The bank believes the partnership will help promote digital payments, innovation, and customer satisfaction. Additionally, Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank recently introduced a flexible travel package installment plan for its credit cardholders, allowing them to pay tour package costs in monthly installments over 6 to 12 months.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Partners with Hospitality and Health Institutions to Offer Exclusive Discounts
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL), embracing the motto “Strong Bank, Successful Cooperation”, has partnered with various hospitality, health, and restaurant service providers to offer exclusive discounts to its debit card, credit card, and mobile banking users. The collaboration benefits customers across multiple outlets, promoting convenient and value-added services. Additionally, the bank recently launched a facility allowing credit card holders to purchase travel packages with flexible 6–12 month installment plans.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Re-Certified with ISO 9001:2015 for Quality Excellence
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has been re-certified with the internationally recognized ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System. The certification, initially effective from August 16, 2024, was renewed following a successful surveillance audit in Bhadra 2082. Under the category of “Provision of Development Banking Activities,” MLBL remains a leading development bank in achieving this global standard.
The re-certification acknowledges the bank’s strong commitment to maintaining international quality benchmarks, delivering excellent customer service, ensuring client satisfaction, and continuously improving operational efficiency. The comprehensive audit evaluated the bank’s policies, procedures, documentation, and overall management practices. With the motto “Strong Bank, Successful Co-operation,” Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank has been providing quality financial services across Nepal for 31 years, serving over 800,000 customers nationwide.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Partners with Radisson Hotel to Offer Special Discounts for Travelers
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has signed an agreement with Radisson Hotel Lazimpat to provide special discounts to its customers at the Radisson Airport Lounge inside Tribhuvan International Airport. The collaboration aims to benefit travelers, especially during festivals and international trips, while strengthening partnerships in the hospitality and health sectors.
Under the agreement, customers using Mahalaxmi Bank’s debit cards, credit cards, or mobile banking can enjoy various discounts, 15% on Radisson Airport Lounge services, 20% on food and beverages (including Izakaya Hokkaido Hotel), 15% on pastry purchases and Tranquility Spa services, and 20% on gym services at Dyson Fitness Center.
The bank believes this initiative will directly benefit its customers and enhance their travel experience. Additionally, Mahalaxmi Bank recently launched a new travel package payment plan, allowing credit cardholders to purchase tour packages through travel agencies and repay the amount in flexible installments over 6 to 12 months.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Launches Startup Loans for Returning Nepali Migrant Workers
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has introduced a special startup loan program aimed at Nepali migrant workers returning from abroad, helping them become successful entrepreneurs. Targeting individuals with skills, experience, and some savings but lacking sufficient investment, the loan supports businesses in agriculture, trade, services, and production. Loans range from NPR 10 lakh to 1 crore, with a repayment period of 2 to 15 years, offered at competitive interest rates.
The initiative aims to promote self-reliance among returnees, generate local employment, foster entrepreneurship, and ensure productive use of remittances, contributing to Nepal’s overall economic growth. Existing residents can also access this facility to start or expand small and medium enterprises. MLBL, embracing its motto “Strong Bank, Successful Collaboration,” has served over 800,000 customers nationwide over the past 31 years.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Supports Reconstruction of Damaged Durbarmarg Police Office
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has provided financial assistance for the reconstruction and repair of the Durbarmarg Police Office in Kathmandu, which was damaged during recent protests involving arson and vandalism. The support aims to help the police office quickly resume normal operations by facilitating essential civil works and maintenance.
The bank believes this contribution will significantly aid the ongoing reconstruction efforts. MLBL also confirmed that all its services, including digital banking, are operating smoothly across its 102 branches (except the Lakeside branch), continuing its commitment to delivering quality financial services nationwide.

Headline: MLBL Condoles Tragic Losses, Ensures Continued Banking Services Amid Crisis
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) expressed deep sorrow over the recent tragic incidents that caused loss of life, injuries, and damage to government, public, and private properties. The bank extended condolences to the bereaved families and wished a speedy recovery for the injured.
While the bank’s Lakeside, Pokhara branch building was completely damaged, banking services from this branch are being provided through nearby branches. All other 102 branches and digital services are fully operational. MLBL also expressed hope that the ongoing government formation process will soon restore peace, good governance, a stable business environment, economic stability, and security across the country.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Partners with Institutions to Offer Special Discounts for Customers
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL), under the motto “Strong Bank, Successful Partnership”, has signed agreements with various institutions, including hospitals, restaurants, diagnostic centers, hotels, and resorts, to provide special discounts to customers using its debit/credit cards and mobile banking services. Through this collaboration, customers can enjoy direct benefits such as reduced prices on healthcare services, dining, accommodation, travel, and shopping. The bank believes this initiative will enhance customer satisfaction while promoting digital financial services. Additionally, MLBL has launched an installment plan for credit card holders to purchase tour packages from travel agencies with flexible repayment terms ranging from 6 to 12 months.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Launches Credit Card Travel Packages for Festive Season
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has introduced a new facility allowing customers to purchase travel and tour packages using its credit cards, targeting the upcoming festive season. Recognizing the growing trend of Nepalis traveling abroad during festivals, the bank has partnered with reputable travel agencies, including Guru Travels Ltd. and Recent & Rhythm Tours, for this service.
Customers can convert the total cost of their tour packages into flexible monthly installments ranging from 6 to 12 months, with no EMI processing fees. This initiative promotes digital payments and enhances festive experiences. Additionally, MLBL recently added a virtual credit card feature to its mobile banking app, Mahalaxmi Smart Saathi, strengthening its commitment to providing secure and convenient banking services to over 8 lakh customers through 103 branches nationwide.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Wins Prestigious International Award, Strengthens Cross-Border Banking with HDFC
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) was honored with the prestigious "Assets Quality" award by the Indian Chamber of Commerce, Kolkata, at the 3rd Emerging Asia Banking Conclave and Awards held in New Delhi on August 29, 2025.
Recognized for its effective asset management and quality improvement, the award enhances the bank’s international reputation. Recently, MLBL also partnered with India’s HDFC Bank to facilitate cross-border financial services, enabling customers to make payments from India to Nepal.

Headline: Comprehensive Analysis of Fourth Quarter Reports for FY 2081/82: A Closer Look at Development Banks in Nepal
Full Content:
The fourth-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2081/82 have been publicly disclosed by 15 out of 16 development banks. These reports provide a comprehensive overview of their financial health. Karnali Development Bank Limited has not published its report as Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has declared it a "problematic institution" and placed its management under direct NRB control. Share trading of Karnali Development Bank has also been suspended.
This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited third-quarter reports for the 2081/82 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) currently lists 16 development banks, divided into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our focus is on assessing the performance of these "B" class financial institutions, drawing insights from the recently released quarter-end reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period, amounting to Rs. 153.74 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit, which amounts to Rs. 131.04 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs.68.86 Crores. In terms of growth in net profit, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) achieved the highest growth margin of 201.97% for Q4 of FY 81/82.
At the regional level, Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported the highest growth in net profit at 287.60% for Q4 of FY 81/82.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.04 Arba among all the development banks, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) holding the second-highest paid-up capital at Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reported the highest reserve and surplus, totaling Rs. 4.92 Arba. Following MNBBL is Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) with a reserve of Rs. 3.03 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) holds the third position with a reserve of 2.9 Arba.
Meanwhile, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU), and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
Among B-class institutions, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with a total deposit of Rs. 1.17 Kharba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a deposit of Rs. 90.12 Arba. The overall development banks have collected a total deposit of Rs. 4.1 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
As of Q4 2081/82, total loans and advances of development banks reached Rs. 4.82 Kharba, with an average loan of Rs. 32.18 Arba. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) disbursed the highest loan amount, totaling Rs. 97.52 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 69.32 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) disbursed Rs. 546.93 Arba, ranking third.
Net interest income:
In terms of Net Interest Income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with Rs. 4.55 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 3.64 Arba, and Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank  with Rs. 2.24 Arba. Out of the 15 banks, 8 reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside funds as loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments for several borrowers.
Total impairment charges amount to Rs. 4.47 Arba for loans and other losses. Among National Level banks, Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) shows the highest impairment charge at Rs. 128.34 Crores, with Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) also holding high provisions at Rs. 67.97 Crores.
At the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported a reversal in impairment charges.
Annualized Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the annualized EPS list at Rs. 23.07 per share, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) followed by  with Rs. 21.82 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) at Rs.192.73 per share, followed by Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) with Rs. 169.95 per share and Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) at Rs.168.13 per share. The average net worth per share of the 15 banks is Rs.137.55.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio indicates how much investors are paying for each rupee of the firm’s earnings. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio at 18.57 times, whereas Jyoti bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) reports the highest P/E ratio at 1248.34 times.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loans indicate credit risk for banks. Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest NPL ratio at 0.28%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest at 50.97%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reported the highest CAR at 31.54% while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reported the negative CAR at 7.84%.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 6.61%, while Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest at 3.87%.
CD Ratio:
The Credit-Deposit Ratio shows how much deposit money has been used as loans. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) reports the highest CD ratio of 89.62%, and Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has the lowest at 63.04%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
The base rate, the minimum interest rate banks charge, is highest at Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) with 16.24% and lowest at Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) with 6.02%. Meanwhile, Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reports the highest interest spread rate of 4.60%, and Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has the lowest at 3.96%.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Partners with HDFC to Launch Cross-Border Payment System from India to Nepal
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has partnered with India’s leading financial institution, HDFC Bank, to launch a cross-border payment system allowing direct transfers from India to Nepal. With this, MLBL becomes the first development bank in Nepal to implement such a system.
The service uses HDFC’s advanced Cash Management System (CMS), enabling transfers via NEFT, RTGS, and FT directly into MLBL accounts in Nepal, along with cheque deposits from other Indian banks.
This partnership strengthens banking ties between Nepal and India and supports smoother cross-border trade and remittance services. The bank has also added a virtual credit card feature to its mobile banking app "Mahalaxmi Smart Sathi" and continues expanding digital innovations across its 103 branches and 800,000 customers.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Strengthens Community Ties Through Nationwide CSR Efforts
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank carried out diverse CSR initiatives in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2081/82, focusing on education, health, hygiene, and social welfare.
Major efforts included distributing school bags to needy students in Bajura, funding toilet construction in Baitadi, and donating food supplies to an old age home in Kanchanpur.
The bank also provided scholarships, refreshments, and artificial limbs, partnering with Rotary Clubs for school infrastructure projects.
These activities reflect the bank’s dedication to inclusive and sustainable community development. With over 100 branches, 49 ATMs, and 800,000+ customers, Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank continues to lead in financial services, digital innovation, and social impact across Nepal.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Pioneers Nepal’s First Virtual Credit Card Among Development Banks
Full Content:
Fonepay, Nepal’s leading digital payment network, in collaboration with Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank, has introduced the Mahalaxmi Fonepay Credit Card — the first of its kind by any development bank in the country.
Entirely virtual and accessible via the bank’s mobile app “Mahalaxmi Smart Sathi,” this credit card enables customers to make QR-based payments at Fonepay-enabled merchants nationwide. Users will enjoy traditional credit card benefits, including a 45-day interest-free period and flexible repayments, without the need for a physical card.
To mark the launch, users can avail up to 50% cashback (maximum Rs. 500) on their transactions for a limited time.
This initiative reflects a significant move toward redefining digital credit access and underscores the growing shift toward inclusive, tech-driven financial services in Nepal.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Launches Fully Digital Virtual Credit Card
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank, in partnership with Fonepay, has launched a fully digital virtual credit card service through its mobile banking app “Mahalaxmi Smart Sathi.” Customers can now make secure and convenient payments via Fonepay QR merchants and online shopping without the need for a physical card.
The virtual card offers similar features as a physical credit card, including a 45-day interest-free period and flexible installment options. To encourage usage, the bank is offering up to Rs. 500 cashback for users of the virtual card.
With this launch, Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank becomes the first development bank in Nepal to introduce such a service, further strengthening its position in digital innovation.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Celebrates 31st Anniversary with Employee Honors and Toastmasters Launch
Full Content:
On the occasion of its 31st anniversary, Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank honored 26 employees who have dedicated 20 years of service with honesty, professionalism, and responsibility. The recognition ceremony took place in Kathmandu, attended by the bank’s Chairman, Board of Directors, CEO, and staff members from various branches.

Full Content:

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Marks 31st Anniversary with Nationwide Programs Honoring Women Entrepreneurs, Health Initiatives, and Cultural Events
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank celebrated its 31st anniversary with a week-long series of programs from Jestha 4 to Jestha 10, 2082. As part of the celebration, the bank honored women entrepreneurs across its branches nationwide to promote financial inclusion, economic growth, social progress, and gender equality. Additionally, on Jestha 6, the bank organized a large-scale blood donation drive across 10 major branches and the central office, collecting 320 pints of blood to support healthcare needs.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Joins NEPALPAY Card Scheme to Boost Domestic Card Services
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited has signed an agreement with Nepal Clearing House Limited (NCHL) to become a principal member of the National Card Switch and Domestic Card Scheme (NEPALPAY Card). The partnership will enable the bank to issue and acquire NEPALPAY Cards following the commercial rollout.
This initiative is part of Nepal’s effort to develop a central infrastructure for domestic card transactions, reduce reliance on international card systems, promote data localization, and enhance digital innovation. Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Introduces Nepal’s First Inter-Bank Scan2Cash Service and Cross-Border QR Payment for Tourists
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has launched Nepal’s first inter-bank Scan2Cash service in collaboration with Fonepay, allowing customers to withdraw cash by scanning a QR code at teller counters using any bank's mobile banking app. Initially available at the bank’s Durbarmarg and Thapathali branches, the service will be expanded nationwide.
This innovation aims to reduce dependency on cheques and ATM cards. Additionally, the bank has enabled cross-border QR payments through the Alipay+ network, allowing tourists from China, Singapore, South Korea, and other countries to make payments in Nepal using their home country's digital wallets via NEPALPAY QR. To further strengthen its digital services, the bank has also launched an upgraded mobile application named “Mahalaxmi Smart Sathi.”

Headline: Insightful Evaluation: Q3 2081/82 Performance Analysis of B-Class Development Banks Unveiled
Full Content:
The third-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2081/82 have been publicly disclosed by 15 out of 16 development banks. These reports provide a comprehensive overview of their financial health. Karnali Development Bank Limited has not published its report as Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has declared it a "problematic institution" and placed its management under direct NRB control. Share trading of Karnali Development Bank has also been suspended.
This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited third-quarter reports for the 2081/82 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) currently lists 16 development banks, divided into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our focus is on assessing the performance of these "B" class financial institutions, drawing insights from the recently released quarter-end reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Garima Bikas Bank (GBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period, amounting to Rs. 73.35 Crores. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit, which amounts to Rs. 72.49 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 51.40 Crores. In terms of growth in net profit, Jyoti Bikas Bank (JBBL) achieved the highest growth margin of 101.15% for Q3 of FY 81/82.
At the regional level, Corporate Development Bank (CORBL) reported the highest growth in net profit at 103.90% for Q3 of FY 81/82.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) holding the second-highest paid-up capital at Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reported the highest reserve and surplus, totaling Rs. 4.10 Arba. Following MNBBL is Garima Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) with a reserve of Rs. 3.03 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) holds the third position with a reserve of 2.9 Arba.
Meanwhile, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU), and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
Among B-class institutions, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with a total deposit of Rs. 1.13 Kharba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a deposit of Rs. 85.79 Arba. The overall development banks have collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.95 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
As of Q3 2081/82, total loans and advances of development banks reached Rs. 4.77 Kharba, with an average loan of Rs. 31.83 Arba. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) disbursed the highest loan amount, totaling Rs. 96.03 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 69.05 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) disbursed Rs. 54.73 Arba, ranking third.
Net interest income:
In terms of Net Interest Income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with Rs. 3.28 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 2.66 Arba, and Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE) with Rs. 1.93 Arba. Out of the 15 banks, 8 reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside funds as loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments for several borrowers.
Total impairment charges amount to Rs. 5.07 Arba for loans and other losses. Among National Level banks, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) shows the highest impairment charge at Rs. 123.38 Crores, with Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) also holding high provisions at Rs. 94.89 Crores.
At the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported a reversal in impairment charges.
Annualized Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the annualized EPS list at Rs. 17.22 per share, followed by Sindhu Bikas Bank Limited (SINDU) with Rs. 18.76 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) at Rs. 180.24 per share, followed by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) with Rs. 163.86 per share and Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) at Rs. 163.22 per share. The average net worth per share of the 15 banks is Rs. 133.69.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio indicates how much investors are paying for each rupee of the firm’s earnings. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio at 22.99 times, whereas Corporate Development Bank Limited reports the highest P/E ratio at 422.72 times.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loans indicate credit risk for banks. Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest NPL ratio at 0.78%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest at 44.96%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reported the highest CAR at 34.19% while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reported the negative CAR at 1.14%.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 7.04%, while Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest at 4.21%.
CD Ratio:
The Credit-Deposit Ratio shows how much deposit money has been used as loans. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) reports the highest CD ratio of 87.95%, and Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has the lowest at 69.29%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
The base rate, the minimum interest rate banks charge, is highest at Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) with 15.51% and lowest at Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) with 6.92%. Meanwhile, Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reports the highest interest spread rate of 4.60%, and Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has the lowest at 4.01%.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Offers Eco-Friendly Home Loan at 7.99% Interest for New Year 2082

Full Content:

has launched the digital version of its "Mahalaxmi Calendar 2082" during an event at the bank's central office in Durbarmarg. Additionally, the bank has launched the "Mahalaxmi Smart Partner" mobile app to offer advanced and secure digital banking services.

Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) reaffirmed its commitment to sustainable banking by organizing a two-day annual program and a heritage conservation walkathon on Falgun 15-16, 2081. Full Content:

Dolma Consultancy, with experience in collaborating with national and international banks, will help strengthen MLBL’s loan recovery system and improve bad debt management.

Full Content:

Headline: Comprehensive Analysis of First Quarter Reports for FY 2081/82: A Closer Look at Development Banks in Nepal
Full Content:
The first-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2081/82 have been publicly disclosed by all 16 development banks. These reports provide a comprehensive overview of their financial health. This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited first-quarter reports for the 2081/82 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) currently lists 16 development banks, divided into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our focus is on assessing the performance of these "B" class financial institutions, drawing insights from the recently released quarter-end reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period, amounting to Rs. 28.18 Crores. Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) comes in second place in terms of profit, which amounts to Rs. 23.94 Crores.
The third position is secured by Garima Bikas Bank (GBBL) with a net profit of Rs. 22.57 Crores. In terms of growth in net profit, Jyoti Bikas Bank (JBBL) achieved the highest growth margin of 197.62% for the Q1 of FY 81/82.
At the regional level, Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported the highest growth in net profit at 1100.52% for Q1 of FY 81/82.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) holding the second-highest paid-up capital at Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reported the highest reserve and surplus, totaling Rs. 3.81 Arba. Following MNBBL is Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a reserve of Rs. 3.52 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) holds the third position with a reserve of 3.39 Arba.
Meanwhile, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU), and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
Among B-class institutions, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with a total deposit of Rs. 1.10 Kharba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a deposit of Rs. 83.27 Arba. The overall development banks have collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.9 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
As of Q1 2081/82, total loans and advances of development banks reached Rs. 4.74 Kharba, with an average loan of Rs. 29.65 Arba. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) disbursed the highest loan amount, totaling Rs. 94.72 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 68.42 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) disbursed Rs. 53.74 Arba, ranking third.
Net interest income:
In terms of Net Interest Income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with Rs. 1.11 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 98.68 Crores, and Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE) with Rs. 65.89 Crores. Out of the 16 banks, 8 reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside funds as loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments for several borrowers.
Total impairment charges amount to Rs. 1.85 Arba for loans and other losses. Among National Level banks, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) shows the highest impairment charge at Rs. 38.77 Crores, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) also holding high provisions at Rs. 37.21 Crores.
At the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported a reversal in impairment charges.
Annualized Earnings per share:
Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) topped the annualized EPS list at Rs. 22.97 per share, followed by Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE) with Rs. 20.23 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) at Rs. 196.57 per share, followed by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) with Rs. 163.48 per share and Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) at Rs. 154.21 per share. The average net worth per share of the 16 banks is Rs. 129.64.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio indicates how much investors are paying for each rupee of the firm’s earnings. Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio at 23.75 times, whereas Corporate Development Bank Limited reports the highest P/E ratio at 520.44 times.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loans indicate credit risk for banks. Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest NPL ratio at 1.80%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest at 34.81%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) reported the highest CAR at 34.95%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reported the lowest at 4.58%.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest Cost of Funds at 7.82%, while Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest at 4.92%.
CD Ratio:
The Credit-Deposit Ratio shows how much deposit money has been used as loans. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reports the highest CD ratio of 87.72%, and Karnali Development Bank Limited (KRBL) has the lowest at 59.81%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
The base rate, the minimum interest rate banks charge, is highest at Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) with 16.32% and lowest at Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) with 7.59%. The average interest spread among development banks remains consistent at around 4.59%.

Headline: Global IME Bank and Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Sign Agreement for Non-Fund Based Banking Facilities
Full Content:
Global IME Bank Limited and Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank have entered into an agreement to offer non-fund based banking facilities. This agreement was formalized by Surendra Raj Regmi, the Chief Executive Officer of Global IME Bank Limited, and Dipesh Lamsal, the Chief Executive Officer of Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank. It enables Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank customers to access services such as letters of credit, bank guarantees, and trade transaction banking through Global IME Bank.
Celebrated as one of the top banks in Nepal by the Euro Money Award for Excellence 2024, Global IME Bank boasts an extensive network of over 1,000 service centers, which include branches and ATMs across all 77 districts. Established in 2052, Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank serves more than 800,000 customers through its 103 branches and 49 ATMs, promoting its services under the slogan "Strong Bank, Successful Cooperation."

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Launches Enhanced "Mahalaxmi Smart Sathi" App for Convenient Digital Banking Ahead of Festive Season
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank
has launched a refined mobile application called "Mahalaxmi Smart Sathi" in alignment with Nepal Rastra Bank’s objectives for the upcoming Dashain, Tihar, and festive season. The app offers advanced, secure, and user-friendly digital banking services. It includes several new features not found in traditional banking apps, such as:
1. Real-time fixed deposit collateral loan of up to Rs. 8,00,000, a first among development banks in Nepal.
2. Online KYC form submission and updates.
3. The ability to apply for savings and fixed deposit accounts online.
4. Self-assessment of loan eligibility and loan application submission via the app.
The app aims to increase banking access in rural and semi-urban areas, promoting financial inclusion while reducing the need for in-person visits to the bank. Available on both Apple Store and Play Store, the app will automatically update on users' devices. For more details, customers can contact 9847387524. The bank has been serving Nepal with 103 branches and over 8 lakh customers for the past 30 years under the motto "Strong Bank, Successful Partnership."

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Enhances Digital Banking Security with Visa Ready Facility
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank has introduced the dollar and N. P. Visa Ready facility to enhance the security of online transactions for customers using R cards. This makes Mahalakshmi Bikas Bank the first among Nepal's development banks to offer such a feature.
The new system will authenticate transactions with a one-time password (OTP) sent via email or message, ensuring that card details are not misused.
This initiative aims to provide modern, safe, and convenient digital banking services while protecting customers' financial information from unauthorized access.
The implementation of 3D security features will reduce online fraud and enable real-time transaction verification, allowing customers to shop securely on thousands of e-commerce platforms globally. With 103 branches and around 8 million customers, the bank has been committed to delivering quality financial services for the past 30 years.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Honors Chaniklal Tamang for Heroic Rescue Efforts
Full Content:
Chaniklal Tamang, a 33-year-old resident of Temal village in the Kavre district, was honored by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank for his heroic act of rescuing two individuals at Nakhu Khola.
During a ceremony at the bank's central office on the 13th Ashwin, he received a cash award of Rs. 1 lakh. The bank hopes that recognizing such bravery will inspire others to participate in rescue efforts during disasters.
Additionally, Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank expressed condolences to those affected by recent floods in the country and wished for the quick recovery of the injured.
The bank has been providing quality financial services to Nepalese people for 30 years under the slogan "Strong Bank, Successful Cooperation."

Headline: Muna Aryal Honored with the 21st Mahalaxmi Literature Award
Full Content:
The 21st edition of the Mahalaxmi Literature Award for the year 2080 was awarded to epic poet Muna Aryal on 2081/06/05.
Originally established by Yeti Finance Limited (now merged with Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank) in 2059 B.S., the award aims to honor significant contributions to language and literature.
The event, organized in collaboration with Matribhumi Sahitya Samaj, Makwanpur, was chaired by Krishna Prasad Dahal, with Bagmati Province Home Affairs and Law Minister Suraj Chandra Lamichhane as the chief guest.
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank hopes this initiative will support the development and preservation of Nepal's literary sector, in line with its mission of providing quality financial services for over 30 years.

Full Content:

Adhyanta Fund Management will offer technical support in areas such as financial investment, market expansion, and business development, while Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank will facilitate capital access and provide financial services in line with Nepal Rastra Bank's regulations.

Full Content:

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Partners with Round Table Nepal for Environmental and Educational Initiatives
Full Content:

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Partners with Pioneer Moto Corp for Special Vehicle Loans

Headline: Financial Showdown: A Comparative Deep Dive into Development Banks' Q4 Performance for FY 2080/81
Full Content:

This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited fourth-quarter reports for the 2080/81 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) currently lists 16 development banks, divided into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our focus is on assessing the performance of these "B" class financial institutions, drawing insights from the recently released quarter-end reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period amounting to Rs. 1.27 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit which amounts to Rs. 1.13 Arba.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 69.74 Crores. In terms of growth in Net profit, Shangrila Development Bank (SADBL) has obtained the highest growth margin of 92.47% for the Q4 of FY 80/81.
Coming towards the regional level, Corporate Development Bank (CORBL) has reported the highest growth in net profit of 194.23% for Q4 of FY 80/81.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
The reserve is the amount that is retained by the company from its profits to promote future growth.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest reserve and surplus which amounts to Rs. 3.50 Arba. MNBBL is followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a total reserve of Rs. 3.26 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) has secured the third position with a reserve of 3.11 Arba.
Whereas, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
In B-class institution, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has topped the list with a total deposit of Rs. 1.09 Kharba. This list is followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a total deposit of Rs. 84.25 Arba.
The overall development bank has collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.94 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Till Q4 2080/2081, total loans and advances of development banks stood at Rs. 4.61 Kharba. The average loan stood at Rs. 30.78 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has disbursed the highest amount of loans which amounts to Rs. 91.90 Arba. Following the list, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has disbursed a total loan of Rs. 66.01 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) has disbursed a loan of Rs. 52.17 Arba which puts it in third place.
Net interest income:
Net Interest Income is the core business revenue which is calculated by subtracting the cost related to the deposits from the income from loans and advances.
In terms of Net interest income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) tops the list with a total of Rs. 4.18 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest net interest income amounting to Rs. 3.46 Arba. GBBL is followed by Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) which has reported a net interest income of Rs. 2.36 Arba.
Out of the 16 banks, 8 banks have reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside a certain amount in loan loss provision and have delayed the loan repayment of several borrowers. A total of Rs 3.83 Arba has been shown in an impairment charge for a loan and other losses.
In the National Level, Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has the highest impairment charge for a loan and other losses with Rs. 95.17 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) also has higher provisions amounting to Rs. 70.92 Crores.
In the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) have reported the lowest impairment charges for this period.
Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the list in terms of EPS amounting to Rs. 20 per share. Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has the second-highest EPS with Rs. 18.38 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) with Rs. 188.48 per share. This is followed by Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) with a net worth per share of Rs. 164.48 per share. Similarly, Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) reported a net worth of Rs. 160.44 per share.
The average net worth per share comes at Rs. 133.10 per share when we factor in the net worth per share of 16 banks.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio tells investors what they are paying for each rupee of earnings of the firm. The lower the ratio, the better the deal.
In terms of the P/E ratio, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio of 19.25 times. Meanwhile, Narayani Development Bank Limited reported the highest P/E of 685.79 times.
One should always check the fundamentals of the company and if they find the bad fundamentals then there is a reason for the lower valuation. Also, the PE is calculated as per the quarter-end closing price of the respective companies. In today's date, the price differs in the secondary market.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loan indicates the risk of credit provided by the bank to its clients. A higher NPL indicates that the bank might be at risk.
In terms of NPL, Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest ratio with an NPL of 0.97%, and on the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has reported the highest NPL of 35%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
In terms of the Capital Adequacy ratio (CAR), Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) seems to have reported the highest CAR of 38.65%, while Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) has the lowest CAR of 6.58%.
CAR is the ratio of a bank's capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets and current liabilities.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
The term cost of funds refers to how much banks and financial institutions spend in order to acquire money to lend to their customers. The lower the cost of funds, the better because it ultimately reduces the cost of banks. As per reports, Corporate Development Bank Limited (LBBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 7.71%, whereas Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest cost of funds at 5.55%.
CD Ratio:
The CD ratio refers to the credit-deposit ratio in banking parlance. It tells how much of the money banks have raised in the form of deposits has been deployed as loans. Similarly, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest CD ratio of 85.83%, whereas Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has reported the lowest CD ratio of 60.56%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
Base rate is defined as the minimum interest rate set by the NRB below which banks are not permitted to lend to their customers. Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reports the highest base rate of 15.33%, and Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest base rate of 8%.
Likewise, the net interest rate spread represents the variance between the interest rate disbursed to depositors and the interest accrued from loans extended to consumers by a bank. Among the majority of development banks, a consistent interest spread rate of 4.58% has been upheld, with the highest reported at 4.59%.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Introduces Single-Digit Interest Rates on Diverse Loan Products
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank is offering a range of loans at a single-digit interest rate of 9.99%, including:
1. Mahalaxmi Home Loan: Up to Rs. 5 crores for residential, commercial real estate, or home renovations, with repayment terms from 2 to 30 years.

Headline: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Introduces QR Code Loan Application Service
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank has introduced a QR code-based loan application facility, enhancing its digital and automated service offerings. This initiative marks the bank as a leader among development banks in Nepal for such services.
Customers can now apply for loans by scanning QR codes available on the bank's official platforms, branch offices, and newspapers.
After application, branch staff will assist customers through the loan process at their chosen branch.
Celebrating 30 years with the motto "Strong Bank, Successful Cooperation," the bank continues to provide doorstep service to Nepalese citizens. The bank's 22nd annual general meeting has resolved to seek strategic partnerships with foreign banks or financial institutions.

Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL), in collaboration with PhonePe, continues to offer international QR payment services, enabling Indian citizens in Nepal to make instant, secure, and convenient payments at various commercial stores. Utilizing QR codes provided by the bank, Indian payment services like Bhim Pay, Paytm, and GooglePay facilitate seamless transactions across Nepal.
This initiative aims to enhance economic, social, and bilateral relations between Nepal and India while fostering economic and tourism development in Nepal. The Mahalaxmi Corporate Cricket League 2024 concluded with Prime Commercial Bank Limited clinching the championship title, and ICFC Finance Limited securing the second place. Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) has embraced eco-friendly practices by introducing electric vehicles for its office use during the Jeshtha month and in celebration of its 30th annual festival and World Environment Day.

Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) is celebrating its 30th year by organizing the Mahalaxmi Corporate Cricket League-2024, Edition 3, from Jestha 22nd to 24th at Ballpark Sports Events and Academy in Imadol, Lalitpur.
This prestigious cricket league involves banks and financial institutions licensed by Nepal Rastra Bank and features 16 teams from various institutions.

The Narayangadh branch donated Rs. 300,000 to Galeshwar Ashram in Devghatdham, Tanahu, to aid in completing the temple premises. The bank plans to continue various social and economic transformation programs as part of its CSR efforts.

Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL), celebrating its 30th anniversary with the slogan "Strong Bank, Successful Cooperation," has been providing accessible and quality financial services to Nepalese people for three decades.

Full Content:

Full Content:

On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.

The reserve is the amount that is retained by the company from its profits to promote future growth.

The overall development bank has collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.65 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Till Q2 2080/2081, total loans and advances of development banks stood at Rs. 4.59 Kharba. The average loan stood at Rs. 30.59 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has disbursed the highest amount of loans which amounts to Rs. 96.30 Arba. Net Interest Income is the core business revenue which is calculated by subtracting the cost related to the deposits from the income from loans and advances.

In the regional level, Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) have reported the lowest impairment charges for this period.

Headline: Comprehensive Analysis of First Quarter Reports for FY 2080/81: A Closer Look at Development Banks in Nepal
Full Content:
The disclosure of first-quarter reports for the ongoing fiscal year 2080/81 from all 16 development banks offers a detailed understanding of their financial standing. This in-depth analysis will specifically focus on evaluating the financial performance of the "B" class financial institution, Development Banks of Nepal.
Currently listed on NEPSE, there are a total of 16 development banks. However, not all of the banks fall under the same category. The development banks can be categorized into two subcategories, National-level banks, and Regional-level banks. Therefore, our examination will center on dissecting the performance of B-class financial institutions based on the unaudited 1st quarterly report of the 2080/81 fiscal year.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period amounting to Rs. 22.88 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit which amounts to Rs. 20.15 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 19.17 Crores. In terms of growth in Net profit, Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank (KSBBL) has obtained a growth margin of 188% for the Q1 of FY 80/81.
Coming towards the regional level, Karnali Development Bank (KRBL) has reported the highest growth in net profit of 149.15% while Excel Development Bank (EDBL) reported the highest decline in net profit of 737% in the Q1 of FY 80/81. As per reports, 12 companies have reported a decline in net profit for this period.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 6.42 Arba among all the development banks. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 5.19 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
The reserve is the amount that is retained by the company from its profits to promote future growth.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest reserve and surplus which amounts to Rs. 3.2 Arba. MNBBL is followed by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) with a total reserve of Rs. 2.74 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has secured the third position with a reserve of 2.73 Arba.
Whereas, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
In B-class institution, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has topped the list with a total deposit of Rs. 1.16 Kharba. This list is followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a total deposit of Rs. 78.36 Arba. Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has secured the third position with a total deposit of Rs. 61.81 Arba.
The overall development bank has collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.63 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Till Q1 2080/2081, total loans and advances of development banks stood at Rs. 4.54 Kharba. The average loan stood at Rs. 28.37 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has disbursed the highest amount of loans which amounts to Rs. 96.74 Arba. Following the list, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has disbursed a total loan of Rs. 63.02 Arba. Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has disbursed a loan of Rs. 51.13 Arba which puts it in third place.
Net interest income:
Net Interest Income is the core business revenue which is calculated by subtracting the cost related to the deposits from the income from loans and advances.
In terms of Net interest income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) tops the list with a total of Rs. 1.04 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest net interest income amounting to Rs. 88.83 Crores. GBBL is followed by Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) which has reported a net interest income of Rs. 57.40 Crores.
Out of the 16 banks, 8 banks have reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside a certain amount in loan loss provision and have delayed the loan repayment of several borrowers. A total of Rs 1.91 Arba has been shown in an impairment charge for a loan and other losses.
In National Level, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest impairment charge for a loan and other losses with Rs. 36.15 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) also has higher provisions amounting to Rs. 35.35 Crores.
In the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has reported the lowest impairment charges for this period.
Earnings per share:
Karnali Development Bank Limited (KRBL) topped the list in terms of EPS amounting to Rs. 32.50 per share. LBBL Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) has the second-highest EPS with Rs. 20.49 per share.
Out of 16 development banks, 12 banks have reported above-industry average EPS.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) with Rs. 181.07 per share. This is followed by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) with a net worth per share of Rs. 157.38 per share. Similarly, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) reported a net worth of Rs. 152.71 per share.
The average net worth per share comes at Rs. 128.33 per share when we factor in the net worth per share of all the 16 banks.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio tells investors what they are paying for each rupee of earnings of the firm. The lower the ratio, the better the deal.
In terms of the P/E ratio, Karnali Development Bank Limited (KRBL) has the lowest P/E ratio of 7.95 times. Meanwhile, Corporate Development Bank Limited reported the highest P/E of 105.53 times from the regional level.
One should always check the fundamentals of the company and if they find the bad fundamentals then there is a reason for the lower valuation. Also, the PE is calculated as per the quarter-end closing price of the respective companies. In today's date, the price differs in the secondary market.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loan indicates the risk of credit provided by the bank to its clients. A higher NPL indicates that the bank might be at risk.
In terms of NPL, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the lowest ratio with an NPL of 1.49%, and on the other hand, Saptakoshi Development Bank Limited (SAPDBL) has reported the highest NPL of 18.50%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
In terms of the Capital Adequacy ratio (CAR), Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) seems to have reported the highest CAR of 44.92%, while Karnali Development Bank Limited (KRBL) has the lowest CAR of 10.10%.
CAR is the ratio of a bank's capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets and current liabilities.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
The term cost of funds refers to how much banks and financial institutions spend in order to acquire money to lend to their customers. The lower the cost of funds, the better because it ultimately reduces the cost of banks. As per reports, Green Development Bank Limited (GRDBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 9.99%, whereas Sindhu Bikas Bank Limited (SINDU) has the lowest cost of funds at 8.36%.
CD Ratio:
The CD ratio refers to the credit-deposit ratio in banking parlance. It tells how much of the money banks have raised in the form of deposits has been deployed as loans. Similarly, Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has reported the highest CD ratio of 93.07%, whereas Karnali Development Bank Limited (KRBL) has reported the lowest CD ratio of 75.78%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
Base rate is defined as the minimum interest rate set by the NRB below which banks are not permitted to lend to their customers. Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reports the highest base rate of 17.78%, and Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest base rate of 12%.
Similarly, the net interest rate spread is the difference between the interest rate a bank pays to depositors and the interest rate it receives from loans to consumers. Here,Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest interest spread of 5.12%.

Headline: NRB Reports Net Profits of Commercial and Development Banks Till Bhadra of FY 2080/81; GBIME Leading The Chart
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has unveiled recent statistics covering the net profit of commercial banks, and development banks for up to the first two months of the current fiscal year 2080/81 i.e. Bhadra.
Commercial Banks
During the first two months of the fiscal year 2080/81, commercial banks in Nepal collectively earned a total net profit of Rs. 16.64 Arba.
Among these, Global IME Bank earned the highest net profit, surpassing all others, with Rs. 1.75 Arba. Similarly, Nabil Bank earned Rs.1.56 Arba, NIMB earned Rs. 1.48 Arba, Himalayan Bank earned Rs. 1.23 Arba, and Kumari Bank earned Rs. 1.14 Arba in net profits during this period. These five banks stood out with profits exceeding Rs. 1 Arba.
On the other hand, Nepal SBI Bank and Machhapuchchhre Bank reported the lowest net profits during this period, with Rs. 27.29 Crores and Rs. 37.63 Crores, respectively. Citizens Bank earned Rs. 44.31 Crores and Standard Chartered Bank reported a net profit of Rs. 48.45 Crores.
The net profit of other banks remained above Rs. 50 Crores.
Development Banks
The development banking sector in Nepal achieved a noteworthy net profit of Rs. 1.35 Arba, despite facing losses reported by four out of the 17 banks in this category. Muktinath Bikas Bank emerged as a standout performer, recording an impressive net profit of Rs. 31.28 crore, closely followed by Garima Bikas Bank, which earned Rs. 16.55 crore.
Conversely, Green Development Bank and Salapa reported the lowest profits in the sector, with earnings of Rs. 1.03 Crores and Rs. 40.10 Lakhs, respectively. Additionally, Narayani, Saptakoshi, Excel, and Miteri Development Bank faced challenges as they grappled with net losses during the period.

Headline: Net Profit of Development Banks of Nepal Has Decreased In Q3; Dive Into Comprehensive Analysis of Major Indicators For All 15 Development Banks In Nepal
Full Content:
Without a doubt, the Financial Institutions are also experiencing economic instability as a result of market swings, given the increasing interest rates, inflation, and overall worldwide recession. Financial institutions' primary business revenue may be affected as a result of the monetary policy's higher interest rate bar, which may be advantageous for some financial institutions and detrimental for others. In this comprehensive analysis, we will examine the  financial performance of “B” class financial institution; Development Banks of Nepal, and see which institution is maintaining a good financial position despite numerous obstacles.
There are 16 development banks which are currently listed NEPSE. However, the Quarter third report (Q3) of
Saptakoshi Development Bank Limited (SAPDBL)
is not yet published by the company. Hence, this analysis discards SAPDBL.
So, let’s dissect the performance of B-class financial institutions based on the unaudited 3rd quarterly report of 2079/80 fiscal year.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report,
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has reported the highest net profit for the period amounting to Rs. 80.63 Crores.
Garima Bikas Bank Limited(GBBL)
comes in second place in terms of profit which amounts to Rs. 65.19 Crores.
The third position is secured by
Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE)
with a net profit of Rs.
55.45
crores. In terms of growth in Net profit,
Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE)
has obtained growth margin of 14.39% for the Q3 of FY 79/80.
Coming towards regional level,
Corporate Development Bank Limited(CORBL)
has reported highest growth in net profit of 73.10% in the Q3 of F.Y 79/80. As per reports, 9 companies have reported decline in net profit for this period.
Paid up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 6.42 Arba among all the development banks.
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
has the second-highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 5.19 Arba.
On the other hand,
Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC)
has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs.26 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
Reserve is the amount that is retained by the company from its profits to promote future growth.
Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL)
has reported the highest reserve and surplus which amounts to Rs. 2.6 Arba. JBBL is followed by
Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL)
with a reserve of Rs. 2.5 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has secured the third position with a reserve of 2.4 Arba.
Whereas,
Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC)
has reported negative reserves and surplus amounting to Rs.10 Crores.
Deposits from Customers:
In B-class institution,
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has topped the list with a total deposit of Rs. 1.12 Kharba. This list is followed by
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
with a total deposit of Rs. 73.87 Arba.
Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL)
has secured the third position with a total deposit of Rs. 57.52 Arba.
The overall development bank has collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.24 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Till Q3 2079/2080, total loans and advances of development banks stood at Rs. 4.30 Kharba. The average loan stood at Rs. 28.73 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has disbursed the highest amount of loans which amounts to Rs. 91.85 Arba. Following the list,
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
has disbursed a total loan of Rs. 60.66 Arba.
Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL)
has disbursed a loan of Rs. 49.29 Arba which puts it in third place.
Net interest income:
Net Interest Income is the core business revenue which is calculated by subtracting the cost related to the deposits from the income from loans and advances.
In terms of Net interest income,
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
tops the list with a total of Rs.3.03 Arba.
Garima
Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
has the second-highest net interest income amounting to Rs. 2.38 Arba. GBBL is followed by
Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL)
which has reported a net interest income of Rs. 1.68 Arba.
Out of the 15 banks, 8 banks have reported above industry average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside a certain amount in loan loss provision and have delayed the loan repayment of several borrowers. A total of Rs 4.29 Arba has been shown in an impairment charge for a loan and other losses.
In the national level,
Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL)
has the highest impairment charge for a loan and other losses with Rs. 77.9 Crores.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
also have higher provisions amounting to Rs. 71.5 Crores.
In the regional level,
Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC)
has reported the lowest impairment charges for this period.
Earnings per share:
Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE)
topped the list in terms of EPS amounting to Rs. 18.45 per share.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has the second-highest EPS with Rs. 17.26 per share.
Out of 15 development banks, 8 banks have reported above industry average EPS.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by
Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL)
with Rs. 173.67 per share. This is followed by
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL)
with a net worth per share of Rs. 152.81 per share. Similarly,
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL)
reported a net worth of Rs. 148.33 per share.
The average net worth per share comes at Rs. 130.12 per share when we factor in all the net worth per share of all the 15 banks.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio tells investors what they are paying for each rupee of earnings of the firm. The lower the ratio, the better the deal.
In terms of the P/E ratio,
Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL)
has the lowest P/E ratio of 17.61 times. This means that you are paying Rs. 17.21 for every Rupee of earning of Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited.
Corporate Development Bank Limited
reported highest P/E of 144.47 times from the regional level.
One should always check the fundamentals of the company and if they found the bad fundamentals then there is a reason for the lower valuation. Also the PE is calculated as per the quarter end closing price of the respective companies. In today's date the price differs in the secondary market.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loan indicates the risk of credit provided by the bank to its clients. Higher NPL indicates that the bank might be at risk.
In terms of NPL,
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has the lowest ratio with an NPL of 1.99% and on the other hand,
Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL)
has reported the highest NPL of 8.92%.
Out of 15 banks, 9 banks have reported below industry average NPL for this quarter.
One should calculate the industry average in terms of their own analysis model
.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
In terms of Capital Adequacy ratio (CAR),
Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL)
seems to have reported the highest CAR of 51.83%, while
Karnali Development
Bank Limited (KRBL)
has the lowest CAR of 10.20%.
CAR is the ratio of a bank's capital in relation to its risk weighted assets and current liabilities.
Others:
Cost of Funds:
The term cost of funds refers to how much banks and financial institutions spend in order to acquire money to lend to their customers. The lower the cost of funds, the better because it ultimately reduces the cost of banks. As per reports,
Green Development Bank Limited (GRDBL)
has the highest Cost of Funds of 11.01%, whereas
Narayani Developmen
t
Bank Limited (NABBC)
the lowest cost of funds of 8.37%.
CD Ratio:
The CD ratio refers to the credit-deposit ratio in banking parlance. It tells how much of the money banks have raised in the form of deposits has been deployed as loans. Similarly,
Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL)
has reported highest CD ratio of 96.28%, whereas
Karnali Development
Bank Limited (KRBL)
has reported  the lowest CD ratio of 75.56%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
Base rate is defined as the minimum interest rate set by the NRB below which banks are not permitted to lend to their customers.
Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC)
reports the highest base rate of 17.01%, and
Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL)
has the lowest base rate of 12%.
Similarly, the net interest rate spread is the difference between the interest rate a bank pays to depositors and the interest rate it receives from loans to consumers. Here,
Karnali Development
Bank Limited (KRBL)
has the highest interest spread of 4.94%.
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates and Interest Spread:

Headline: Banks and Financial Institutions Reduce Interest Rates for Baishakh
Full Content:
Banks and Financial Institutions have unveiled the interest rates profile for the month of Baishakh.
Commercial Banks:
The Chief Executive Officers of commercial banks' umbrella group, NBA, lowered the interest rates which shall be effective from Baishkah, 2080.
It has been decided to reduce the interest rate on personal deposits by 10%. The interest rate on fixed deposits has now decreased to single digits as a result of this move.
For commercial banks, the interest rate of one-year term deposits has decreased from 11 percent to 9.9 percent.
Along with this, the interest rate of institutional fixed deposits has remained at 7.99 percent. Similarly, the interest rate on savings has remained at 5.4 to 7.4 percent.
The rate of remittance has been maintained at an average of 10.99%.
Development Banks:
Development Bankers Association, an association of Development Bank Chief Executive Officers, also lowered the interest rate. The members of the committee have resolved to lower the deposit interest rate by 1%.
Now the interest rate on personal term deposits is 10.60 percent and the institutional term deposit interest rates have been lowered to 8.60 percent for a period over one year.
The average interest rate for remittance has been maintained at 11.60 percent.
Additionally, the savings interest rate has been reduced by 0.60 percentage points so the interest rates on savings of development banks will be 6 percent to 9 percent.
Finance Companies:
For the finance companies, the rates effective from Baishakh shall be 10.60 percent – 10.75 percent for individual fixed deposits. The average rates of the same for institutions is 8.75%.
On the other hand, the average interest rates for remittance has been maintained at 11.60-11.75 percent.
The interest rates on savings for finance companies has been maintained at an average rate of 8-9%.
